svg.title: Agentic AI abuse of GitHub-exposed app secrets kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: GitHub secret search for exposed application credentials; service principal sign-ins to Entra ID from 199.19.77.84 and Tor exit 199.19.77.18; Azure Resource Manager credential harvesting; adaptive retry with corrected api-version; pivot through a single-tenant OAuth app to Key Vault, VM Run Command, AI resources and Graph content; response. Critical stages are sign-in, ARM harvesting and the pivot. Detection anchors are Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3 and PEAK hunts H1-H3.
svg.text: Agentic AI tooling abuses GitHub-exposed app secrets to take over Entra and Azure
Vendor: Microsoft (2026-11-05) | Date: 2026-11-11 | Cluster: unattributed (low) | Day 141
ENTRA ID TENANTS AND AZURE, AUG-OCT 2026
Discovery: large-volume GitHub secret searches for a target's app credentials and AI keys [T1593.003 T1552.001]
From August 2026 the agent queries GitHub combining org name, secret keywords, cloud-service and AI-provider keywords
Targets: OAuth / application credentials and AI inference API keys left in public repos (Entra client secrets, 8Q~ format)
No actor named by Microsoft; framework class = ARTEX-style agentic offensive tooling (nmap, curl, Playwright, Python)
GitHub code search -> client_secret, tenant id, AI provider keys
Service principal sign-ins with the leaked secrets, mostly from 199.19.77.84 and Tor exit .18 [T1078.004]
From as early as 2026-10-28; dozens of applications across multiple tenants, one IP hitting several service principals
Invalid or expired secret failures (AADSTS7000215 / AADSTS7000222) mean someone holds a credential for the app
Failure then success from the same IP is the urgent pattern; sign-ins are non-interactive, no user MFA is involved
ARM credential harvesting and enumeration: storage keys, app settings, connection strings, AKS [T1555.006 T1580]
Operations that return secrets: storage account keys, publishing credentials, AI/ML connections and datastores, AKS user creds
Enumerates subscriptions, resource groups, permissions, AI model deployments and service configuration
Control-plane POST actions (list*) appear in Azure Activity; plain GET reads generally do not
listKeys listCredentials listPublishingCredentials listClusterUserCredential
Adaptive retry: HTTP 400 on a wrong api-version, same call resent 28-80 s later returns 200 [automation signal]
Seen for Key Vault secret metadata, Azure SQL firewall rules GET and an Application Insights query (api-version 2023-07-01)
Behaviour of an agent that reads the error and self-corrects, not of a fixed script; IP and user-agent blocks will not stop it
Microsoft notes default tool user agents can show in traffic; 65.87.223[.]26 sent shell commands inside a user agent
400 -> corrected api-version -> 200 in under 2 min 65.87.223[.]26 157.22.126[.]128
Pivot via a single-tenant OAuth app: Key Vault, Azure DevOps, VM Run Command, AI, Graph [T1528 T1651 T1530]
GitHub secret search to Key Vault exfiltration took five minutes in one case; Azure DevOps searched for further secrets
Compromised OAuth app used with Azure VM Run Command (credential exposure, persistence, lateral movement); AI resources validated
SharePoint / OneDrive files downloaded and mailbox items accessed via Microsoft Graph, mostly searches
Key Vault secret list/get VM runCommand Graph search one app: ARM + KV + Storage + Graph tokens
Response and break points [no technique]
Rotate every exposed secret, remove all app credentials (including attacker-added), revoke sessions, rotate Key Vault contents
Alert on service principal sign-ins from unseen IPs, 3+ SPs from one IP, and credential-returning ARM operations by SPs
Prevent: no secrets in repos, push protection, managed identities, app management policies, Conditional Access for workload IDs
Entra app secrets | ARM list* ops | Key Vault audit | GitHub secret scanning
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA (2 hygiene rules), Suricata sids 9990001-9990003, PEAK H1-H3. IPs published by Microsoft; may rotate.
Break points: secret rotation, SP sign-in anomaly, ARM list* by SPs, Key Vault audit. Hashes, domains and exact user agents not published.
